Triggers.value: Visible injuries or wounds on others

Threat.value: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
I wake during the night to check whether I am safe

Memory.value: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop

Negative Appraisals.value: You can never know who will harm you
I can't trust that I will do the right thing
I have permanently changed for the worse

vignette: Sofía, a 27-year-old Latin American woman working as an HVAC technician, has experienced profound psychological distress following a traumatic event involving torture. Sofía’s symptoms have progressively worsened over time, leading her to seek help after months of debilitating experiences. The incident occurred when she was kidnapped and held captive for several days by individuals who subjected her to brutal physical abuse and psychological torment. The trauma was compounded by the absence of any means to escape or call for help, leaving Sofía feeling completely trapped and vulnerable. These memories have left a lasting impact on her daily life, affecting both her professional and personal experiences. Sofía's triggers—being alone with women, seeing visible injuries or wounds on others, and situations where she feels she has no options—are all potent reminders of the traumatic event. The memory of being held captive by women who inflicted pain upon her has left her hyper-vigilant in the presence of other females. This hyper-vigilance is further exacerbated when she encounters visible injuries or wounds on others, as these remind her of her own suffering and vulnerability. The trauma has deeply affected Sofía’s perception of safety and control. She now checks repeatedly that doors and windows are locked, and she frequently wakes up in the middle of the night to ensure her surroundings remain secure. Her jumpy startle response is also a constant reminder of the fear and unpredictability she experienced during the traumatic event. When memories of the torture resurface, Sofía feels an intense sense of shame, believing that she somehow failed to prevent or escape from the situation. These memories often feel alien to her, as if they do not truly belong to her own experience. The overwhelming emotional response to these intrusive recollections has led Sofía to avoid situations where such memories might be triggered. Sofía’s negative appraisals—her fear that anyone could harm her, doubts about her ability to make the right decisions, and belief that she is permanently damaged—have become central to how she navigates daily life. These beliefs fuel her heightened sense of threat, as they lead her to constantly monitor her environment for potential dangers. Her self-doubt has also made it difficult for her to trust her own judgment or actions. For instance, during her work as an HVAC technician, being alone with female clients can trigger intense feelings of fear and vulnerability. Sofía finds herself constantly checking the locks on doors and windows in these situations, feeling that she cannot predict who might harm her next. Her sense of entrapment is magnified by the realization that she could be working in a space where escape options are limited. The cycle of negative appraisals and threat perception has become self-reinforcing over time. Sofía’s fear that anyone can harm her leads her to be overly cautious, which then triggers more intrusive memories and feelings of shame. These memories, in turn, exacerbate her sense of vulnerability and further fuel her constant monitoring for threats. This cycle has taken a toll on both her personal life and professional relationships. She has distanced herself from female colleagues and friends, feeling that being alone with them might trigger intense anxiety. This isolation has led to strained relationships at work and difficulty forming close bonds outside of it. Ultimately, Sofía’s increasing sense of helplessness and fear about the future brought her to seek help. While she is most afraid of reliving the trauma and feeling vulnerable again, she also hopes for a way to reclaim some control over her life and find a path towards healing from these experiences.
